key_insight: The paper reframes workflow generation as a knowledge modeling problem, using hierarchical reasoning to produce more coherent and executable ComfyUI-style workflows.
engineering_relevance: For modeling and simulation pipelines, this suggests that agentic systems should reason over modular structure and workflow knowledge rather than generating JSON directly from text.
method: Knowledge inversion: distill real workflows into hierarchical representations from pseudo-code and skeletons to high-level strategies.
Knowledge injection: supervised fine-tuning teaches task-to-strategy and strategy-to-executable-structure reasoning.
Inference: reversible reasoning plus self-refinement improves structural coherence and workflow validity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive experiments showing richer node diversity, more coherent structures, and higher execution success rates than existing systems.
watch_item: The approach depends on high-quality workflow corpora and careful multi-stage training/inference, which may increase system complexity and deployment cost.
